terra.problem: The text says the Rabshakeh stopped by the aqueduct, not that the army went straight to the king's door.
“Wrong turn” calls the baker's answer wrong.
It states the Rabshakeh's mood as fact rather than marking it as Papa Dorin's impression.
It invents a reason the Rabshakeh does not use the word “wise.”
Pharaoh is the Egyptian king's title, not a personal name given in the passage.
The Rabshakeh says the splintered staff pierces the hand, not that it breaks.
The passage does not say the staff breaks; it says the splintered staff pierces the hand.
It gives an unstated reason for the Rabshakeh's claim: that he is using the LORD's name to push Judah around.
The officials ask him not to speak Hebrew in the people's hearing. The text does not say they want the talk kept between officials or that the men on the wall are listening.
It states that the officials are worried without marking that feeling as a guess.
The text says he called out loudly in Hebrew, but does not say the people on the wall could hear him just fine.
The text says the people remained silent; it does not say that the gates stayed closed or that nothing was opened.
The text says the officials relayed the Rabshakeh's words, not that they told Hezekiah everything they had heard.
The text reports that the officials relayed the Rabshakeh's words, but does not say they asked for nothing.
